header.name: Nation and her Narratives
header.description: This course introduces students to the literature of India. It surveys a selection of literary works by authors in India and in the diaspora. The course will examine how key cultural concepts have reappeared across Indian literary traditions over time and how they have been reimagined within the context of specific historical junctures and socio-linguistic networks. It shall focus on themes such as idea of home and territories, women and notion of the body, borders and conflict, power and politics, problems of translation, and the intersections between ideas of real and imagined geographies that constitute the dynamics of the Indian literary scape. In studying some specific sections, there will be the comparative study of constructions of themes in cinematic productions. The idea is to include the discursive, alternate versions of the thematic narration and the kinds of discordant identities they imagine and manoeuvre from the text or screen to the layers of socio-cultural literary articulation.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Student should be able to approach a literary text for identifying relevant issues in historical and contemporary contexts, appreciate diversity of artistic expressions, Identify and define literary elements, genres, and other elements of literary narration

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Ask informed questions, discuss interpretations of literary texts, engage in critical understanding of contexts ideas and share insights with others in group discussion

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Critically analyse a text, creating mind map based on your own observations and close reading. In some cases, the students should be able to compare it with the cinematic narration adapted from the same text, or ideas similar to the ones in the chosen text.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to think, write and speak critically and analytically about crucial issues and then write clear, coherent, well-structured short essays using a given text as support to your claims and as illustrations of the informed comments about a literary work

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Have acquired a literary vocabulary and developed an understanding of how to access textual information through, the students should be able to define their own research interest picking themes from the course to ask the essential, self-refective, critical questions that mark every humanist's rich encounter with data.

lecture_topics: Readings: Rabindranath Tagore’s “The Postmaster” and Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay’s “Mahesh”
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Introduction to the “idea of home as a trope in literary narratives”; Introduction to the literary constructs of literary narratives in India, Underlining the socio-historical context Reading and discussion of narratives selected, Pre-reflection and 1 minute memo.

lecture_topics: Readings: Mahasweta Devi’s “Behind the Bodice” and, Ismat Chughtai’s “The Homemaker”
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Conceptualising the subaltern, Reading and discussion of narratives selected, Pre-reflection and 1 minute memo. discussing on the politics of the body, gender and social marginalisation. 1 minute memo
First assignment on the techniques of transition from the textual to the visual medium based on the same narrative. 1 minute memo

lecture_topics: Shadow lines of Borders and Territories
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Locating the text in context, Discussion of narratives selected, Teasing out the central themes, Critical discussion of the resources, Articulation of individual perspectives, Appreciating the form content relation. Taking notes of different data available on partition of 1947. 1 minute memo

lecture_topics: Critical visualisation of the data: Digital Mapping of the text and the context
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Second assignment on understanding the range of data in the humanities to define, organise information about a data set, and produce visual representations of data. 1 minute memo

lecture_topics: Reading: Amitav Ghosh’s “Ghosts of Mrs. Gandhi”
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: selected, Teasing out the central themes, Critical discussion of the resources, Articulation of individual perspectives, Appreciating the form content relation. Taking notes of different data available on Operation Blue Star, Assassination of Mrs. Gandhi, Sikh riots of 1947, and the situations in Delhi. 1minute memo

lecture_topics: Comparative analysis of intercultural contexts: Working on a similar narrative from any other country
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Third Assignment Group discussion: Intercultural Literary Intervention. What perspectives do we focus through a reading of these diverse contexts?Could we say that approaching the "other" would essentially imply consciously cultivating some knowledge (rather working knowledge) of the other? Does Literature provide the liberty of accessing the other and the unfamiliar, yet see the similarities and parallels of human life and living? 1minute memo

lecture_topics: Reading: Jhumpa Lahiri’s “Mrs Sen’s” and Rohinton Mistry’s “Squatter”.
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Understanding the theoretical and social relevance of the issues in diaspora, Discussion of text, Teasing out the central themes of names, identity, and cultural crossover. 1minute memo

lecture_topics: Micro-conference: short papers from each of the participants
working individually with responses from the faculty
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Fourth Assignment on drafting short papers to present in the form of a seminar on a specific topic with a well defined research question. 1 minute memo
